title: Thomas Wells
text:
I’m an independent data and AI consultant based in Fruita, Colorado. I founded Dynamodal in 2022, and I work mostly as a subcontractor with consulting teams that need an experienced, hands-on data person, and I take on direct client work too.
I studied physics and electrical engineering at the Colorado School of Mines, then spent several years in Alaska’s oil fields before moving into data science consulting. Before Dynamodal, I was on the data analytics and modeling team at a national consulting firm, delivering scenario modeling and analysis for utility and government clients on everything from grid modernization to energy efficiency evaluation.
I’ve worked with data for about two decades and with R for nearly as long. Along the way I’ve done a lot of IT work too, and that’s where I’m most useful: between the people who want to do ambitious analysis and the systems, policies, and tools that have to support it.
These days my work centers on four things: analytics and scenario modeling, especially for energy efficiency and electrification; helping teams adopt AI tools and coding agents with clear eyes about the risks; designing data models and platforms that hold up; and making teams more efficient through better documentation, workflows, and habits.
When I’m not working, I’m usually on a bike, running, or out on the trails and rivers around Fruita. I also run Fruita Tech Wizard, a small side project helping neighbors with their everyday tech.

Practical help where data, tools, and people meet


 Analytics & modeling
Energy efficiency analysis and program evaluation, electrification planning, and systems and scenario modeling. Clear, defensible numbers your team and your client can act on.


 AI for analytics teams
AI assistants and coding agents can multiply what a team gets done, or quietly add new risks. I help teams choose the right tools, set sensible guardrails, and build habits that stick.


 Data strategy & platforms
Data model design, platform migrations, and the practical decisions that make analytics reliable, maintainable, and acceptable to IT.


 Team efficiency
Internal documentation, knowledge bases, reproducible workflows, and the small “work hacks” that give a team hours back every week.

I bridge what analysts need and what IT can support
My background runs through physics, electrical engineering, field work in Alaska’s oil fields, and years of energy consulting, with plenty of IT along the way. That mix lets me translate between what analysts and data scientists want to do, what the tools can actually do, and what IT will allow. Then I find a path that works for all three.
